title: The Use of Spies
coreMove: Pay for human foreknowledge before committing lives and resources to ignorance.
sourcePressure: The source argues that a small outlay for intelligence prevents massive public loss, says foreknowledge comes from people rather than spirits or calculation, names five spy classes, values converted spies, secrecy, rewards, and historical servant-advisers behind dynastic rise.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing spying to sneaky behavior, gossip, or data dashboards.

sourceAnchors.name: five classes of spies
sourceAnchors.detail: Local, inward, converted, doomed, and surviving spies each provide different access to enemy knowledge.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Foreknowledge is not one channel; it is a system of people placed at different distances from the truth.

sourceAnchors.name: I Chih
sourceAnchors.detail: The rise of the Yin dynasty is tied to I Chih, who had served under the Hsia.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: I Chih matters because the decisive knowledge crossed from inside the old order into the new one.

sourceAnchors.name: Lu Ya
sourceAnchors.detail: The rise of the Chou dynasty is tied to Lu Ya, who had served under the Yin.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Lu Ya carries the same warning: inside knowledge can move history when rulers are willing to value it.
